critical_code_review_comments: routers/collection.upload_photos_b64: image validity check uses Image.open(...).verify() which consumes the file object. That's fine for validation but note this bypasses PIL's decode step; a real render (Image.open(...).load()) would catch broken JPEGs that verify() lets through. Low priority since the frontend also decodes into a canvas before base64.

geotag.js watermarkPhoto: uses new Image() which shadows possible global Image references but is fine in browser. Consider passing image dimensions to canvas after orientation-correction — EXIF Orientation is NOT applied here, so a portrait phone photo will be rotated 90° in the watermark preview. Consider using createImageBitmap({imageOrientation:'from-image'}) or a small EXIF orientation pass.

Collection.js PhotoModal: base64 upload state 'items' is not cleared if the modal is closed mid-processing; reopening for another activity might briefly show stale previews if 'items' state persisted (it doesn't because component unmounts, but if PhotoModal is ever memoized/kept-alive this becomes a leak).

routers/collection.upload_photos_b64: hardcoded Indonesian error string 'Lokasi wajib diambil bila Anda mengunggah foto penagihan.' is duplicated verbatim in Collection.js — extract into a shared constants module (backend errors.py + frontend messages.js) to avoid drift.

routers/collection.upload_photos_b64: server does NOT redraw watermark when foto_b64 is received (client already watermarked). This means a malicious client could bypass watermark by sending an un-watermarked base64. Consider always re-drawing (Pillow) on the server too — the spec explicitly says raw multipart endpoint 're-draws watermark with Pillow' but is silent on b64; consistency argues for redrawing server-side to guarantee the emerald+gold strip is present.

Collection.js line 277: mapsUrl uses format 'https://maps.google.com/?q=<lat>,<lng>' per iter-6 spec, which SUPERSEDES iter-5 canonical URL (https://www.google.com/maps/search/?api=1&query=…). Confirm this is intentional going forward; some Google clients redirect the short-form correctly on mobile but desktop may open Search rather than Maps app. Not a bug per spec, flagging for awareness.
collection.get_photo (photo streaming): JWT still passed as ?auth=<token> query param — logged/cached risk, unchanged from iter-5. Recommend short-lived signed URL.

context_for_next_testing_agent: Iter-6 GPS/watermark/b64 feature is FULLY working end-to-end. Playwright: use context.grant_permissions(['geolocation'], origin=<frontend_url>) BEFORE navigate, then context.set_geolocation({latitude, longitude, accuracy}). Period must be switched to '2026-09' via [data-testid=period-filter] to see TEST-GEO-001. To simulate 'no location', simply skip clicking ambil-lokasi-btn (state loc=null; even if permission granted, getCurrentPosition isn't called). The maps URL format is the SHORT form 'https://maps.google.com/?q=<lat>,<lng>' per explicit user request in iter-6 (differs from iter-5 canonical form). piexif is required for the pytest suite — installed via pip into /root/.venv but not in requirements.txt yet; main agent should add it. If password 013 is NewPass2026, run _reset_pw.py first to restore.
rca of the issue: N/A — no bug to reproduce; this iteration was a feature-verification pass. The GPS mandatory-if-photo guard is enforced BOTH client-side (Collection.js upload() early-return with toast) AND server-side (upload_photos_b64 400 'Lokasi wajib …'). Base64 flow: canvas watermark → dataURL split(',')[1] → POST /photos-b64 → server decodes, stores via storage.store_processed_photo, records lat/lon rounded 6-decimals + tanggal_foto→status mapping ('Valid' if same day as activity_date else 'Perlu Verifikasi Admin'). All verified live.
